nonCanonical.defect: integer keys encoded in non-ascending order (key 2 before key 1)
keyVersion 1 encoded as tag 2 (unsigned bignum) c2 41 01 instead of untagged integer 01; tags are rejected
keyVersion 1 encoded as half-precision float 1.0 (f9 3c 00); floating point is rejected

assertions: map has exactly six integer keys
keys are encoded in ascending order
changing any identifier changes AAD and makes decryption fail

provenance.source: docs/contracts/crypto-envelope-v1.md, section Domain separation and associated data; RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 (canonical encoding rules)
provenance.generationProcedure: positive bytes are the canonical CBOR encoding of the declared AAD map with integer keys 1..6 in ascending order (unchanged from the original A04 fixture); nonCanonical bytes each encode the same map with exactly one documented canonicality defect (unordered keys, tagged integer, floating-point value)
